claims.conclusion: Suppose 3 of 40 posts carry a label: 3/40=7.5% is the proportion of labeled posts, not a loss of 7.5% of exposure.
conditions: Hypothetical report example
Numerator 3 posts, denominator 40 posts
claims.practical_meaning: Write '3 posts / 40 posts, a post proportion of 7.5%'; do not attach a causal exposure interpretation.

check.when: When annotating Post labels figures
needed: Labeled-post count and total post count
verify: Check the arithmetic of 3/40
Check that the ratio is still named a post proportion
check.if_missing: Without an actual report, explicitly identify this as a teaching hypothetical, not an account measurement.

limits: Not actual account data.

evidence.supports: The report's post-based units support this hypothetical calculation

claims.title: Five of thirty-one days does not mean five days of complete invisibility
claims.conclusion: Suppose an account label is present on 5 of 31 days: the unit is days; this does not mean posts were entirely invisible at every entry point on those 5 days.
conditions: Hypothetical report example
Specified 31-day period with an account label on 5 days
claims.practical_meaning: Record the 5 days and specific label effect; explain duration separately from visibility scope.

check.when: When annotating Account labels duration
verify: Retain days as the unit
Check which entry points and readers are restricted
check.if_missing: Without the label effect, do not infer all-day, sitewide, or zero-exposure consequences.

limits: Not actual account data.

evidence.supports: Account-label day counts and effect explanations

claims.title: Read What it means together with Effect on visibility
claims.conclusion: What it means and Effect on visibility in the report provide label meanings and effects; some restrict recommendations to non-followers, while others concern content warnings, regional restrictions, or other limits. Do not compress them all into the same 'throttling.'
conditions: Specific report labels and explanations
claims.practical_meaning: Record each label name, meaning, and effect, then explain it using precise audience and entry-point wording.

check.when: When organizing or explaining a visibility report
verify: Check whether the effect is a recommendation restriction, warning, regional restriction, or something else
Retain the applicable scope
check.if_missing: Without an explanation, do not invent a uniform penalty.

limits: A label name cannot replace the full effect explanation.

evidence.supports: Report display fields and explanations of label effects

claims.title: A follower friend opening the post does not rule out non-follower recommendation restrictions
claims.conclusion: Asking a friend who follows you to confirm the post opens cannot rule out restrictions on recommendations to non-followers; conversely, having a label does not mean disappearance from every page. Checks should target the scope stated in the report.
conditions: The observer is known to be a follower
The test concerns opening a post, not recommendations to unfamiliar audiences
claims.practical_meaning: Record the reader relationship, entry point, and action for visibility observations; avoid extrapolating from a single opening test.

check.when: When a friend's ability to open a post or a label's existence is used to judge sitewide status
verify: Distinguish opening from recommendation
Distinguish followers from non-followers
Limit conclusions to the observed scope
check.if_missing: Without observations matching the audience and entry point, keep the matter unverified.

limits: This is a checking method based on official scope, not a sitewide empirical finding.

evidence.supports: Official label explanations distinguish specific audiences and effects

claims.title: Save reports and align concurrent changes before correcting or appealing
claims.conclusion: When relevant labels appear, save the reporting period, names, and explanations and compare account or content changes in the same period; use an applicable correction or appeal entry point to address the issue. Today's title change cannot explain last month's aggregate.
claims.practical_meaning: Create chronologically ordered report and change records, retaining original materials needed for corrections or appeals.

check.when: When a report lists relevant labels
verify: Match temporal order
Confirm the submitted issue falls within that label's scope
check.if_missing: Without contemporaneous information, do not identify the latest edit as the cause.

limits: Report aggregates provide clues; they do not automatically prove a single change caused a label.

claims.title: An empty report means only that this report lists no relevant records
claims.conclusion: When no label is listed, you can only say that this report has no relevant records. It is marked best effort, is not a complete causal log of individual impressions, and does not explain why one post lost to another; an empty report cannot establish that every ranking was normal.
conditions: The reporting period read and its best effort scope
claims.practical_meaning: Clearly state 'no records listed,' then turn to content, available analytics fields, and comparison methods.

check.when: When an empty report is used to prove there are no recommendation issues whatsoever
verify: Do not equate no records with verification of every process
Do not reconstruct request-by-request competitive ranking from the report
check.if_missing: Without complete request logs, leave ranking causes unknown.

limits: Empty records are not reverse proof of a hidden penalty either.

evidence.supports: The report's best effort explanation

claims.title: Content can still be improved item by item when visibility clues are absent
claims.conclusion: After finding no visibility clues, check whether the title is clear, the first image shows results, promised materials appear in the body, and important updates are left only in old replies.
claims.practical_meaning: Find specific improvements across four checks: title, first image, fulfillment of promises, and update discoverability.

check.when: When views are low but the report offers no clear clues
needed: Current title, first image, opening, and body
verify: Check whether readers can quickly identify the result
Compare opening promises with actual materials
Move conclusion-changing updates to a discoverable position
check.if_missing: These four editorial checks can be completed even without internal model scores.

limits: Improving content does not diagnose the recommendation cause or guarantee growth.

claims.title: Choose only one main change per comparison
claims.conclusion: When comparing similar tool tests, keep material scale and observation duration as close as possible and change one main variable, such as replacing a decorative cover image with a result comparison; changing topic, format, audience, and timing together makes effects hard to attribute.
conditions: Content tasks and observation conditions are as similar as possible
claims.practical_meaning: First specify the comparison variable and background conditions kept similar, then record results.

check.when: When designing the next posting comparison
verify: Confirm other changes are recorded
Do not attribute gains after multiple changes to one edit
check.if_missing: If conditions cannot be made similar, describe results as directional clues only.

limits: This does not control every change in the recommendation system or audience.

claims.title: Use actual analytics fields and preserve missing values
claims.conclusion: Use analytics already available to the account; if the platform actually provides profile clicks, follows, bookmarks, or other fields, record them according to their definitions, and leave unavailable fields blank.
claims.practical_meaning: Keep visible field names and definitions; do not invent official algorithm scores or fill gaps with substitute metrics.

check.when: When building a posting-analytics record
needed: Fields actually available to the account
Each field's definition and measurement window
verify: Preserve each field's meaning
Distinguish nonexistent fields, unavailable data, and actual zero values
check.if_missing: Leave unavailable fields blank and mark them missing.

limits: Do not assume different accounts have identical available fields.

claims.title: Views are not deduplicated audience, and thread views cannot be summed as people
claims.conclusion: Public view counts are not deduplicated people; the views of individual posts in a thread cannot be summed and called a unique audience.
conditions: When using the platform's public view numbers
claims.practical_meaning: Report each post's views and their definition separately; without a deduplicated metric, do not manufacture a deduplicated total of people.

check.when: When summarizing thread performance or estimating unique readers
verify: Distinguish views from people
Do not infer audience by simply adding across posts
check.if_missing: Without deduplicated data, list only views; do not label them unique readers.

limits: Total views cannot reconstruct a reader's repeat views or views across posts.

evidence.supports: Official view-count definition is not a deduplicated person count

claims.title: Comparison records should first retain content identity and publishing conditions
claims.conclusion: A basic comparison table should record post link, topic, format, publication time, reply or quote status, and external-link location, making it easier to find similar content rather than forcing different tasks together.
claims.practical_meaning: Use one record per post and these conditions to select comparable groups.

check.when: When building a minimal posting-comparison table
verify: Records are sufficient to return to the original post
Compare content with similar tasks and formats
check.if_missing: Mark missing conditions; do not force records into the same sample category.

limits: These are recording recommendations, not official algorithm-scoring fields.

claims.title: 24 and 48 hours are consistent observation points, not independent samples
claims.conclusion: You can record visible data 24 and 48 hours after publication to standardize observation windows; two time points for the same post are tracking records, not two independent posts.
conditions: Record by elapsed time since publication
24 and 48 hours are suggested observation points
claims.practical_meaning: Keep the same ID and two time points for each post; align post age in comparisons.

check.when: When comparing performance after publication
verify: Align by elapsed time
Do not count two time records for one post as two independent posts
check.if_missing: If a time point is missed, record the actual elapsed duration; do not disguise it as the fixed window.

limits: 24/48 hours is a comparison arrangement, not a platform-promised distribution lifecycle.

claims.title: Record shares, replies, profile clicks, follows, and similar metrics by definition; do not fill missing values with zero
claims.conclusion: Record shares, replies, profile clicks, follows, and other metrics actually provided by the platform, interpreting each by its definition; leave unavailable values blank rather than entering zero.
claims.practical_meaning: Record data availability separately from values, preserving field units and windows.

check.when: When cleaning an analytics table or comparing metrics across posts
verify: Confirm zero means an observed zero rather than an unavailable value
Retain names of distinct actions
check.if_missing: Keep unavailable fields null.

limits: Even identically named fields should not be compared outside platform definitions.

claims.title: Account-goal outcomes can supplement exposure metrics
claims.conclusion: Qualified inquiries, useful visits, and other outcomes related to the account's goals are worth recording; content with ordinary exposure may still merit continuing if it attracts target readers.
claims.practical_meaning: Define useful account outcomes beforehand and examine them alongside visible distribution metrics.

check.when: When deciding which topics or content formats to retain
needed: Definitions of qualified inquiries or useful visits
verify: Check the quality and relevance of goal outcomes
Avoid dropping topics solely by view rankings
check.if_missing: Without usable outcome records, do not speculate about commercial or audience value.

limits: This is goal-oriented editorial judgment, not a recommendation-bonus formula.

claims.title: Record trending events, revisions, and known labels as comparison context
claims.conclusion: Also record concurrent trending events, content revisions, and known visibility labels to avoid attributing every change to one edit.
claims.practical_meaning: Attach contextual notes to each post's results and explicitly list potentially confounding changes when explaining comparisons.

check.when: When numbers rise or fall after an edit
verify: Check when changes occurred
Check for other explanations
check.if_missing: If context is incomplete, weaken attribution.

limits: Recording context cannot eliminate all confounding.

claims.title: Use distributions and medians across posts so a viral post does not dominate
claims.conclusion: When comparing multiple posts, inspect distributions and medians to avoid letting one accidentally viral post dominate the mean.
conditions: Multiple comparable posts are available
claims.practical_meaning: Retain per-post data and examine both typical performance and dispersion.

check.when: When comparing overall performance across topics, formats, or changes
verify: Inspect outliers' effects on the mean
Examine the median and distribution
check.if_missing: If samples are few or groups dissimilar, describe individual results honestly rather than forcing a stable pattern.

limits: The original text provides no minimum sample size guaranteed to be reliable.

claims.title: Each impression cannot be treated as an independent random experimental sample
claims.conclusion: The same reader may see content repeatedly, and the platform selects different audiences; a comparison cannot simply treat each impression as an independent, random experimental sample.
conditions: Observational data from organic posting and platform distribution
claims.practical_meaning: Account for dependence involving posts and audience selection; do not use huge impression counts to pretend there are equally many random samples.

check.when: When assessing whether differences are stable or causal
needed: Known limitations from repeated views and audience selection
verify: Distinguish impression records from independent experimental units
State that organic distribution is not a randomized experiment
check.if_missing: Without audience or allocation data, do not claim to have completed a randomized causal experiment.

limits: Controlling content variables still does not control all platform and audience changes.

claims.title: With enough samples, bootstrap intervals at the post level
claims.conclusion: With enough samples, bootstrap intervals can use posts as the unit; with few samples, honestly record direction and uncertainty.
conditions: Multiple posts and a sample sufficient to support the intended comparison
Posts are the resampling unit
claims.practical_meaning: When intervals are needed, resample posts rather than impressions or different time points for the same post, and report sample limitations alongside them.

check.when: When adding uncertainty estimates to a multiple-post comparison
verify: Confirm posts are the resampling unit
Check that a post's 24/48-hour records are not treated as independent samples
Retain small-sample limitations
check.if_missing: If samples are insufficient, record only direction and uncertainty; do not force a precise interval.

limits: The original text gives no universal sample-size threshold.
An interval does not automatically establish causality.

claims.title: A one-month observation schedule has four stages
claims.conclusion: The original report offers this monthly starting schedule: week one, organize the baseline, profile bio, and pinned post; week two, publish complete original work within sustainable capacity; week three, compare only one main variable; week four, review topics that brought relevant readers and actual outcomes.
conditions: Adapt to your own capacity and existing rhythm
claims.practical_meaning: Use the four weeks for preparation, publishing, a single-variable comparison, and outcome review, retaining records for each stage.

check.when: When starting a content-observation cycle
verify: Each week has a clear task
Avoid changing multiple things in week three
In week four, examine both relevant readers and actual outcomes
check.if_missing: If a mature process already exists, use your own baseline; do not disrupt capacity merely to fit this schedule.

limits: This is an experimental arrangement, not an algorithmic requirement.

claims.title: One post daily or three to five weekly is only an experimental starting point
claims.conclusion: The report's example of one post per day, or three to five per week if quality falls, is only an experimental starting point; an established rhythm should retain its own baseline, without presenting these numbers as algorithmic requirements.
conditions: Posting quality and capacity are sustainable
Numbers are examples of observation arrangements
claims.practical_meaning: Adjust frequency according to quality and new information, and record the actual rhythm.

check.when: When a user asks how many posts to publish daily or a draft claims rewards for a fixed frequency
verify: Identify the numbers as examples rather than thresholds
Check whether frequency harms quality
check.if_missing: Without frequency experiments, start with the existing sustainable baseline; do not provide an algorithmically optimal post count.

limits: Not finding a daily-post-count formula does not mean all production limits are known.

claims.title: The OCR publishing example is only an organizational hypothetical using one batch of Chinese invoices
claims.conclusion: The complete publishing example assumes the same batch of Chinese invoices is used to compare two OCR tools; A and B are placeholders demonstrating article organization only, without assuming any test results.
conditions: The same batch of Chinese invoices
Tools A and B are placeholders
No actual results
claims.practical_meaning: Replace the example with real tools, materials, and results when using it, and identify untested areas.

check.when: When turning the OCR example into a publishable article
verify: Confirm placeholder comparison has not been presented as measurement
Results must be supported by actual materials
check.if_missing: Without measured data, keep it as a structural template; do not publish fabricated rankings.

limits: No tool's superiority or inferiority can be inferred from the example.

claims.title: The OCR opening should serve tool selection and manual-verification tasks
claims.conclusion: Readers may be choosing a tool, or already using one and wanting to know which fields still need manual checking. The opening should explain what this test covers, avoiding a broad question such as 'How powerful is AI recognition really?' that the materials cannot answer.
conditions: The described Chinese-invoice OCR comparison example
claims.practical_meaning: Narrow the opening to actual fields and reader decisions; do not generalize to all AI recognition capabilities.

check.when: When drafting an OCR test's title and opening
needed: Scope of conclusions supported by the materials
verify: Check that the text states what was tested
Ensure the title does not exceed the evidence's scope
check.if_missing: If the readers or test items remain unclear, first limit the scope to completed tests.

limits: This is editorial positioning, not a format mandated by the recommendation system.

claims.title: The complete OCR opening draft retains scope, input, and usage guidance
claims.conclusion: Opening draft: 'This comparison covers only dates, tax amounts, and buyer information on Chinese invoices. Both tools use the same batch of original images; error examples and test settings appear below. If you plan to import recognition results directly into your accounting records, first check which fields still require manual verification.'
conditions: Example copy
The body must actually supply the promised materials
claims.practical_meaning: Reuse the structure of scope, identical input batch, evidence location, and reader use case, replacing the test items with real ones.

check.when: When a concrete, usable test-opening example is needed
verify: Verify dates, tax amounts, and buyer information were actually tested
Confirm promised examples and settings can be found in the body
check.if_missing: If any promised material is missing, remove or revise that promise; do not invent results.

limits: This is not a statement that testing has been completed.
It does not constitute a conclusion about specific accounting operations.

claims.title: Test methods should list sample count, version, date, quality, and evaluation method
claims.conclusion: The body should list sample count, tool versions, test date, image quality, and evaluation method; untested types must not enter the conclusions. This makes the test understandable and verifiable; recommendation code does not require every article to follow one format.
conditions: When readers need to understand and verify a test
claims.practical_meaning: Supply all five methodological details near the results and mark the sample boundaries of conclusions.

check.when: When reviewing a comparison test's verifiability
verify: Methods suffice to understand the results
Conclusions do not include untested types
check.if_missing: If methods are missing, state the gaps and narrow conclusions; do not treat untested items as results.

limits: This is editorial and verification advice, not a platform-wide writing template.

claims.title: Use a representative error-versus-correct comparison in the first image and label conditions
claims.conclusion: The first image can show a representative error-versus-correct comparison with test conditions; if the results concern only blurry images, say so on the image rather than presenting a ranking for all invoices. Provide full results and limitations afterward, and retain the main finding in the body.
conditions: Actual, representative test case
Conclusions are limited by input conditions
claims.practical_meaning: Clearly identify the tool/field, incorrect and correct values, and applicable conditions in the first image so the image and body can be cross-checked.

check.when: When selecting the first image for an OCR test
needed: Representative original image and recognition result
verify: The case is not a cherry-picked exception presented as representative
The blurry-image condition is directly visible
The body also states the main finding
check.if_missing: Without a representative real comparison, do not create a conclusion image implying a universal ranking.

limits: The first-image format does not guarantee recommendation gains.

claims.title: Choose a single post, long article, or three-post summary thread by evidence volume
claims.conclusion: One finding with one example can be a single post; when samples, settings, results, and limitations need explanation, retain a long article and create a separate summary thread. If using three posts, the first gives the question and main judgment, the second the comparison, and the third the scope and access to complete materials; include more evidence in full when needed.
conditions: Choose format according to information needs
Three posts is an organizational example
claims.practical_meaning: First ensure the question, judgment, evidence, and boundaries are complete, then decide post count and format.

check.when: When choosing a comparison test's publishing format
verify: Can the information be clearly explained in one post?
Does each of the three summary posts serve a specific purpose?
Do not cut key materials merely to fit three posts when more evidence is needed
check.if_missing: If materials are insufficient, narrow claims; do not create an impression of completeness by increasing post count.

limits: There is no algorithmic guarantee that exactly three posts is optimal.

claims.title: Each summary-thread post should stand alone, with core data not confined to the middle
claims.conclusion: Read each post on its own; expand 'the second problem is more serious' into a specific field and error type. Do not place core data only in the middle of a long thread and assume every Home reader will read from start to finish.
conditions: Thread posts or multiple summary posts may be encountered individually
claims.practical_meaning: Supply the object, finding, and necessary conditions in each post, retaining the main judgment in the first.

check.when: When reviewing individual-post comprehensibility in a long thread
verify: Is it understandable without surrounding context?
Are key numbers hidden only in the middle?
Can references be resolved?
check.if_missing: If context is missing, rewrite the information to be self-contained rather than relying on readers to open the complete thread.

limits: This is editorial advice based on conversation-assembly scope.
Public assembly logic does not guarantee readers see the entire thread.

evidence.supports: Root, ancestor, and current-post assembly and timeline handling do not guarantee full-thread display

claims.title: Examples and conditions promised in the opening must appear in the body
claims.conclusion: If the opening promises error examples, provide original images, recognition results, and correct values; if it promises test conditions, explain versions, inputs, and evaluation methods. Delete paragraphs that repeatedly announce 'the real problem comes later' without adding materials.
claims.practical_meaning: Match each opening promise to its location in the body, replacing previews with verifiable evidence.

check.when: When reviewing promise fulfillment and delaying paragraphs in a test article
needed: Original images, results, and correct values
verify: Each promise can be matched to materials
Reduce repetitive suspense previews
check.if_missing: If materials remain missing, supply them or retract the promise; do not conceal gaps through previews.

limits: This is information-organization advice, not a dwell-time reward technique.

claims.title: Every middle paragraph should add information, with conditions beside conclusions
claims.conclusion: In the middle, check what each paragraph adds; paragraphs repeating the title can be replaced with counterexamples, and conclusions valid only for low-clarity images should place that condition beside them.
claims.practical_meaning: Mark each paragraph's added facts, evidence, counterexamples, or boundaries, and combine purely repetitive paragraphs.

check.when: When shortening or improving the middle of a long test article
verify: Does it add information?
Are conditions adjacent to the conclusions they limit?
check.if_missing: If no information is added, delete or combine paragraphs; do not invent missing counterexamples.

limits: The goal is not simply shorter text or a fixed paragraph count.

claims.title: CREAD cannot choose an article's optimal word count or paragraphing
claims.conclusion: CREAD explains one dwell-time prediction method; it cannot choose the best word count or paragraphing for a particular article. Adjust length to the information each paragraph provides and the reader's task.
conditions: Distinguish prediction methods from editorial choices
claims.practical_meaning: Do not derive guaranteed long-form superiority, a fixed word count, or a fixed paragraphing recipe directly from CREAD terminology.

check.when: When CREAD is used to justify length rules
verify: Check whether the inference jumps from prediction method to optimal length
Review for informational completeness
check.if_missing: Without evidence on length effects, give only editorial reasons; do not call them algorithmic requirements.

limits: The original text provides no universally optimal word count.

evidence.supports: CREAD's multiple thresholds and time reconstruction are prediction methods only; they provide no conclusion on optimal article word count

claims.title: Access to complete comparison materials should deliver promised content and disclose barriers in advance
claims.conclusion: The complete comparison table should have a name, date, and usage instructions; opening the external link should reveal the promised materials, with any registration or payment requirement stated in advance.
claims.practical_meaning: Actually open the materials entry point and verify the content; explain its name, version date, purpose, and access conditions to readers.

check.when: When publishing a test article linking externally to complete materials
verify: The entry point opens normally
The landing page contains the promised content
Access conditions are known before clicking
check.if_missing: If materials are unavailable, repair access or adjust the promise before publishing.

limits: A working link does not mean the platform's internal URL rating is known.

claims.title: Recheck the destination page and link purpose after pinning
claims.conclusion: If this article later becomes a pinned post, periodically confirm that the destination page and link purpose have not changed.
conditions: The article is used as a pinned post or lasting entry point
claims.practical_meaning: When maintaining a pinned post, recheck the final destination, material content, dates, and access requirements.

check.when: When updating a bio or pinned post, or checking long-term access to materials
verify: The link still points to the promised materials
Changes in registration, payment, or purpose are disclosed
check.if_missing: If the destination fails or its purpose changes, repair the link and explanation.

limits: This is maintenance advice, not a guarantee of obtaining or changing the platform's internal reputation.

claims.title: Schedule publication around primary readers' time zones and habits
claims.conclusion: If you know when primary readers look at this type of test, choose a period when they are more likely to be present; 3 a.m. for the author is not necessarily 3 a.m. for the reader.
conditions: Timing information for primary readers is available
claims.practical_meaning: Record readers' time zones and actual reading habits before scheduling or comparing publication times.

check.when: When choosing publication times or explaining late-night posting
verify: Convert to readers' local time
Avoid judging solely by the author's local clock
check.if_missing: Without reader timing information, keep and record the baseline; do not give a universally best time slot.

limits: Timing advice does not guarantee recommendations.

claims.title: Public views cannot calculate the remainder of a 200-view Home quota
claims.conclusion: Public view counts cannot calculate how much of a '200-view Home quota' remains; cold start provides conditional exploration opportunities, not a redeemable guaranteed minimum for every post.
conditions: Public view fields differ from Home count fields
Cold start has additional eligibility and selection conditions
claims.practical_meaning: When explaining low views, do not subtract public views from 200 to calculate a balance; use the named Home field when checking conditions.

check.when: When public numbers are treated as a cold-start progress bar
needed: Cold-start eligibility and actual selection records, if available
verify: Distinguish the two count fields
Confirm conditional exploration is not guaranteed display
check.if_missing: Without the Home field, no remaining allowance can be calculated.

limits: Static conditions cannot guarantee display for a particular candidate.

evidence.supports: Home threshold, jointly required eligibility, and separate Home and general-view fields

claims.title: Reusability, relayability, and accessibility each have independent content value
claims.conclusion: Complete fields, dates, and versions make it easy for readers to return and use the material; a post that clearly explains the test object and purpose is easier for peers to pass along; access to full materials should work normally. These uses need not be converted into 'how many likes they equal' to be valid.
claims.practical_meaning: Check the article and materials entry point against three reader tasks: returning, relaying, and accessing.

check.when: When assessing whether content merits bookmarking, sharing, or long-term maintenance
verify: Returning readers can still identify the applicable version
The content remains understandable independently after someone shares it
The link is accessible
check.if_missing: If information is missing, add what the intended use requires; do not invent engagement-value conversions.

limits: This is an editorial value judgment, not a like-equivalence or recommendation-score formula.

claims.title: Verify questions after publication and publish conclusion-changing findings as separate updates
claims.conclusion: If readers ask whether samples were compressed, verify before answering; if they point out an evaluation flaw, explain what needs correcting. Minor issues can remain in discussion, but conclusion-changing findings should become separate updates with corrections in the original so later readers can find the valid version.
claims.practical_meaning: Distinguish supplementary explanations from corrected conclusions, and clearly connect new updates with corrections in the original.

check.when: When receiving reader questions, counterexamples, or corrections
needed: The samples in question and processing records
Scope of the effect on conclusions
Original text and update entry points
verify: Verify before answering
Explain specific corrections
Both new and returning readers can find the current conclusion
check.if_missing: If verification is pending, state what needs confirmation; do not maintain a definite conclusion whose basis is lost.

limits: Separate updates serve discoverability and accuracy, not guaranteed additional distribution.

claims.title: Keep distribution duration similar in the next comparison and acknowledge remaining changes
claims.conclusion: For the next similar test, you can again change only the results-first image or summary format and allow similar distribution time before comparing; do not compare total counts for a ten-minute-old post with a two-day-old post. This accumulates clues but cannot control every change in the recommendation system and audience.
conditions: Similar content tasks
One main variable
Similar observation duration after publication
claims.practical_meaning: Compare results for posts of similar age, recording uncontrolled background variables.

check.when: When reviewing the next round of first-image or summary changes
verify: Align by elapsed time since publication
Avoid directly comparing 10-minute and 2-day totals
Describe results as clues rather than guaranteed causality
check.if_missing: If durations differ, continue observing or explicitly state that direct comparison is invalid.

limits: Ten minutes and two days illustrate an incomparable situation, not platform thresholds.

claims.title: Whether to publish a third post depends on new information and correction needs
claims.conclusion: After two posts that day, judge a third by what it adds: if it merely rephrases promotion of the first two, consolidate it; if a new test changes the original conclusion, correct it promptly. An unfound daily-post-count formula should not replace this judgment.
conditions: The third post is an editorial-decision example
claims.practical_meaning: Identify the third post's new findings, reader use, or need for correction, then choose consolidation, publication, or revision.

check.when: When deciding whether to keep publishing on the same day
needed: Content of the first two posts
verify: Check whether it is only reworded promotion
Promptly correct substantive errors when found
check.if_missing: Without new information, prioritize consolidation; verify unconfirmed changes first.

limits: Two posts and a third post are not penalty or reward thresholds.
Not finding a formula does not mean all unpublished rules are known.

claims.title: Finally check the first image and opening from an unfamiliar reader's perspective
claims.conclusion: Take the next post's first image and opening on their own: a reader who does not know the author and will not open the full thread should be able to understand what was found and why it matters to them.
claims.practical_meaning: Before publishing, use only the first-screen materials to restate the 'finding' and 'use'; add specifics if they are unclear.

check.when: When completing the final prepublication check
verify: The finding is understandable without the author's background
Its relevance is understandable without opening the complete thread
check.if_missing: If the first screen cannot answer this, revise the first image and opening rather than relying on later sections to reveal the core information.

limits: This is a final editorial check, not an exposure promise.
